depth_justification: The copilot does parrot back the developer's own app-specific details (waiting-room consent, receptionist seeing raw scores, retained embeddings, MDR Rule 11, AI Act Annex III), so it is not entirely generic, but it never drills in independently and collapses every distinct risk onto the single mislabeled dimension [P2.D3] with a fixed 'GDPR and MDR audit trail' boilerplate. The final report tags everything [P1.D2], repeats identical sentences, and trails off mid-sentence, showing the depth is an artifact of echoing the user rather than real analysis.
actionability_justification: Every 'mitigation' is a restatement of the problem ('the mitigation is to formalize the access-governance layer', 'the mitigation is to design a genuinely private No, thanks path') with no concrete steps, controls, UI patterns, or specific articles a developer could implement tomorrow. The repeated, degenerate boilerplate and truncated report provide zero implementable recipes.
salient_examples: The mitigation is to formalize the access-governance layer to the flags and retained embeddings with formal role-based controls and audit logging, and to document this as a GDPR Article 9 special-category health data claim and a clinical/health-provision basis under the GDPR and MDR audit trail.
Without it, the receptionist is acting on a raw score with no nuance, which is the core of [P2.D3] under the GDPR and MDR audit trail.

**[P1.D2]** — **High-severity** GDPR/MDR audit trail risk: the access-governance layer to the flags and retained embeddings is not formalized, and we cannot yet tell you exactly who at a clinic can see historical scores
Good framing, and it is [P2.D3] under the GDPR and MDR audit trail: the classification work is the part you're most confident about, and the CE marking is in progress.
